methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $140M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Panthalassa is a Series B climate and energy company founded by Garth Sheldon-Coulson and Brian Moffat, having raised $140M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 9 private and 1 public company in the climate and energy sector, including KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, Amogy, Helion, and Redwood Materials.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis anchors to the $140M total raised as a proxy valuation and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $266M. Peer-median analysis benchmarks against three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: KoBold Metals at $3.0B (Series C), Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B (Series C), and Amogy at $700M (Series C). The median valuation across these three peers is $1.0B, with a range of $700M to $3.0B.

Triangulating both methods produces a low estimate of $226M, a median of $633M, and a high of $1.1B. The stage-progression method suggests more conservative ground; the peer-median approach reflects higher valuations in the broader climate-tech landscape. Key uncertainties include the degree to which later-stage comparable valuations should discount to a Series B position and the sustainability of current peer valuations in a volatile capital environment. The $633M midpoint represents the most balanced view across methodologies.
